acceptance: Merge-gate evaluation documented for duplicate check runs
Automated mitigation in place (bot rerun of superseded failures or dev-loop guide note) so authors stop hand-rerunning stale failures
context:
Found while landing PRs #2907 and #2913. Workaround used: gh run rerun <failed-run-id>. See handoff _project/handoffs/core-execution-variants-batch-20261009.md revisions 7 and 13.

Update 2026-10-14: the mechanism is now confirmed. The required context `oracle-review` runs on both `pull_request` and `pull_request_review` (.github/workflows/oracle-review.yml:5-10,24-26,30-31), and each run is its own check suite. The `pull_request` run fails by design until a review exists (_project/scripts/oracle_review_check.py:137-146). A later passing `pull_request_review` run does not replace it, and the ruleset requires `oracle-review` without an app pin.
- Seen again on #2940, #2945, #2952 and #2954. On the #2954 head b28d4d95b: failed at 02:42, the review run passed at 02:45, and the PR stayed blocked until a manual rerun at 03:13.
- Fix options:
  - have the trusted review or verdict path rerun the latest failed `pull_request` oracle-review run for the head SHA (needs `actions: write`);
  - or publish `oracle-review` as a commit status from one trusted writer, so the latest result wins, and have the `pull_request` event report pending instead of failure.
description: Twice in the execution-variants effort (PR #2907 run 38189396586; PR #2913 runs 38267710604, 38270039090) the merge gate stayed blocked with two newer same-head SUCCESS check runs present for oracle-review. Running gh run rerun on the failed run replaced it in place and unblocked the merge both times. Suspected mechanism: the gate keys on something other than latest-completed (possibly the dispatch event), unverified.
